prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm operations and maintenance system covers offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel/organizations, communications, cybersecurity, fire protection, backup power through Grid Interface Relay; excludes public grid/unrelated port operations. Objectives: safety, reliability, integrity, availability, environmental protection.
Aliases: Glassfin=Turbine Controller; Morrowick=Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern=Weather Service; Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway; Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine; Amber Quay=Shore Control Room; Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel; Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console; Mosslight=Warehouse System.
Turbine Controller controls turbines, produces Pitch Deviation Notice (recipient unspecified). Equipment: Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone assesses blades. Offshore Substation collects/switches power, contains Main Transformer; Export Cable Monitor monitors export. SCADA Gateway handles supervisory exchanges/access; SCADA Engineer maintains interfaces. Shore Control Room supports Control Engineer monitoring/response. Cybersecurity Gateway bounds connected services. Interfaces have defined responsibilities; supervisory, planning, human-coordination functions remain distinct; personnel retain procedural/safety/engineering authority.
Duty Planner develops daily priorities using Field Supervisor/Maintenance Planning Engine input. Marine Coordinator aligns vessels, crews, port access, locations using Fleet Dispatch Console assignments/movements/status. Weather Service produces Squall Window Bulletin; Metocean Buoy supplies observations; Weather Analyst advises Marine Coordinator. Vessel Master controls navigation/safety/transfer decisions, assesses conditions before/during voyages. Weather Hold pauses affected activity until responsible personnel confirm safe resumption.
Crew Transfer Vessel transports authorized personnel/tools; Daughter Craft supports permitted short-range transfers; Service Operations Vessel supports extended work; Helideck supports helicopters. Warehouse System records stock/prepares equipment/consumables; Storekeeper checks materials, coordinates Spares Hub replenishment. Port Agent arranges vessel calls/crew access/staged cargo. Personnel Tracking Console, North Access Scanner, South Access Scanner support accountability. Work Permit Portal supports authorization. External: grid dispatch, emergency response, communications, port support, suppliers.
Lifecycle: commissioning requires documented handover/verification; routine operation validated status/procedures/forecasts/grid instructions; maintenance weighs condition/resources/access/production/severity; refurbishment; decommissioning safe isolation/removal/record transfer. Require hazard control/accountability, pollution prevention, minimized disturbance, prompt incident response.

New part:
S095: The HSE Officer verifies that work arrangements account for applicable safety controls and personnel responsibilities.
S096: The Field Supervisor coordinates task execution offshore and keeps the Duty Planner informed of changes to work progress.
S097: The Shore Control Room maintains operational oversight and provides a point of coordination for shore-based personnel.
S098: The operating organization uses defined handoffs so that dispatch, marine judgment, work supervision, and stores control remain accountable functions.
S099: The Shore Control Room maintains operational oversight and provides a point of coordination for shore-based personnel.
S100: This section defines how offshore environmental observations and protected operational networks support safe farm operations.
S101: The Metocean Buoy is designated Copper Finch for operational reference.
S102: The Metocean Buoy measures wind speed and direction, wave height and period, current, air temperature, and barometric pressure.
S103: Sensors are selected and mounted to limit exposure to spray, icing, vibration, and corrosion.
S104: An onboard logger timestamps observations and retains a local history during intermittent communications.
S105: The Vessel AIS Receiver produces a Position Quality Flag when position integrity checks fail or confidence falls below its configured threshold.
S106: The Weather Service uses validated environmental observations in forecast products for offshore planning.
S107: The Weather Analyst reviews forecast limitations and identifies conditions that may affect vessel access or turbine work.
S108: Measurement intervals and alarm thresholds are configured to support both trend analysis and timely operational decisions.
S109: Time synchronization and sensor health are checked as part of routine monitoring.
S110: The Cybersecurity Gateway is designated Quiet Harbor for operational reference.
S111: The Cybersecurity Gateway establishes a controlled boundary between authorized shore-side services and offshore operational networks.
S112: The boundary permits only approved protocols, destinations, and service accounts.
S113: External connectivity is denied by default and enabled only for documented operational needs.
S114: The SCADA Gateway remains responsible for supervisory communications within its defined control scope.
S115: Administrative access requires authenticated individual accounts and role-based authorization.
S116: Privileged sessions are time limited, logged, and reviewed against approved maintenance activity.
S117: The Cybersecurity Analyst monitors gateway events for unusual access patterns and configuration changes.
S118: Loss of the security boundary places remote administrative functions in a restricted state without bypassing local protective controls.
S119: Security events are retained in protected logs for investigation and audit.
S120: Network segmentation limits the effect of a compromised endpoint and supports controlled restoration of service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
